chunks: I have truly turned my face towards Him who created the heavens and the earth: I have chosen one way and am not an idolater.

key_terms.حَنِيفاً: a Hanif (one inclined to pure monotheism)
key_terms.وَجَّهْتُ وَجْهِيَ: I turned my face (symbolizing devotion and direction)

ai.seo_question: What does it mean to turn one's face towards the Creator as a Hanif?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse is often cited to highlight the Prophet's (peace be upon him) innate disposition (Fitrah) and his conscious rejection of the idolatry of his contemporaries, establishing the model of pure monotheism. It underscores the concept of Hanifiyyah as a return to the primordial faith of Abraham, distinguishing true submission from mere ritualistic polytheism. This affirmation serves as a theological foundation for the Imamate, where the Imams continue this lineage of pure, unadulterated Tawhid.
